metadata.note: Utility teardown of runtime/scripts/align.py — the 182-line word clock that runs at audio lock (REMOTION.md build-order step 1). Reads narration_text + audio_file from beat_sheet.json, uses faster-whisper (CPU int8) for word-level TIMING only, aligns the KNOWN narration words onto those timestamps via difflib.SequenceMatcher, interpolates the gaps linearly between anchors, pins pre- and post-anchor words to the first/last anchor, and emits mp3/words.json with beat-local startFrame/endFrame at the film fps (metadata.fps overrides ART_FPS_DEFAULT=24). Falls back to even_spread over actual_duration_s (or mp3/timings.json entry, or 0.0) when nothing anchors — with an explicit [warn] print that word-keyed tracks on that beat are unreliable. Three consumers: the Remotion plane, stage_publish.py's SRT cues, the karaoke derivative. Only remote dependency is faster-whisper's initial CTranslate2 model fetch from huggingface.co — with the model cached under ~/.cache/huggingface/hub and HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 to satisfy the sandbox proxy, every demo in demo/RUN-LOG.txt is verbatim on this workstation. Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged for the human reviewer before publication. episode.source_sha256 89e0f38ded269908fab42362723f9dab3d87f449bf08e70cad05a4e4efb3c33e.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK — the word-clock pipeline as a horizontal phase-flow.
beats.narration_text: Here is the pipeline. Take the beat sheet, which already carries the narration text. Take the mp3 files that came out of Kokoro. Feed each mp3 to faster whisper for word level timestamps. Match the recognised words to the known words with SequenceMatcher. Fill any gaps by interpolating between anchors. Emit a single words dot json for the whole reel.

props.heading: The word clock — one pass, one file.
props.body: Beat sheet + mp3 → WHISPER (timing) → MATCH (SequenceMatcher) → INTERPOLATE (gap fill) → EMIT (frame-locked json). One pass. One output. Three downstream consumers.
props.quote: The narration TEXT is already known — it's what the TTS synthesised — so we never transcribe blind: faster-whisper supplies word-level TIMING from each beat's mp3, SequenceMatcher aligns the KNOWN narration words onto those timestamps.
props.sparkLine: Known text · measured audio · one clock.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 4 — even_spread() fallback + the explicit [warn] print. The falsifiability beat.
beats.narration_text: When Whisper anchors nothing — silent audio, non speech, the wrong language — align dot py does not fail the reel. It calls even spread. Words divide the beat duration evenly. It also prints a warning: word keyed tracks on this beat are unreliable. That warning is the point. The clock still exists; the timings on that one beat are averages, not observations. The reel keeps rendering.

props.title: align.py:104-109 + 158-165 — even_spread + [warn]
props.code:
def even_spread(known, duration_s):
    per = duration_s / max(len(known), 1)
    for i, w in enumerate(known):
        w["start"] = i * per
        w["end"]   = (i + 0.9) * per
    return known

# inside main(), after align_words() returns None:
timed = align_words(flat, recognized) if recognized else None
if timed is None:
    if not dur:
        print(f"[skip] {bid}: no alignment and no duration to spread over")
        continue
    timed = even_spread(flat, float(dur))
    n_fallback += 1
    print(f"[warn] {bid}: NO anchors — even spread over {dur}s "
          f"(word-keyed tracks on this beat are unreliable)")
props.sparkLine: Fallback exists. Warning exists. Rendering continues.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the whole file, in the order it does its job.
beats.narration_text: So — align dot py. The word clock. It ingests known text and measured audio, produces a per word timeline in frames at the film fps, and refuses to guess when the audio disagrees. It runs at audio lock, between generate audio and render. Rerun it whenever a beat's mp3 changes. One narration, three consumers: the Remotion plane, the SRT publisher, the karaoke overlay. Exact text. No drift.

props.artifactHeading: align.py — the whole surface, in the order it does its job
artifactLines: input — beat_sheet.json (narration_text + audio_file per beat) + mp3/*.mp3 already generated.
recognise — faster-whisper (CPU int8, base model default) supplies word-level TIMING only.
align — SequenceMatcher matching-blocks anchor known words onto whisper seconds; norm() lowers punct/case.
interpolate — linear gap-fill between anchors; pre-first and post-last pin to the nearest anchor.
emit — mp3/words.json with beat-local startFrame/endFrame at metadata.fps (default 24).
fallback — no anchors + known duration → even_spread + explicit [warn]; no anchors + no duration → [skip].
